items.evidence: After `page.reload()` the spec checks that `nameInput` has the value "E2E Zip Hoodie" and that the header contains it (product-rename.spec.ts:97-99). Both values come back from the server, so the test fails if the save never happened.
Criterion 1, the title after saving, is asserted at spec:93. Criterion 2, the field and the title after a reload, is asserted at spec:98-99.

No existing page object covers the product page. `findProductId` is a new lookup by SKU modelled on `findOrderId` and goes through `gql`/`adminToken` from lib/graphql.ts. It does not copy an existing helper.
There are no fixed waits. `rename` waits for the new name to appear in the header, and `goto` waits for the name input.
The spec uses `test` from fixtures/test.ts and is not tagged `parallel()`. It writes nothing to the cache or the dumps.

It uses the test ids `page-header`, `product-general-settings` (both exist in src) and `button-bar-confirm`. Name is a role locator scoped to the general-settings card, and the header text lookup is scoped to the header. Using `button-bar-confirm` unscoped follows the existing page objects.
The product comes from the existing orders scenario (PRODUCTS.hoodie). The only API call is a read-only id lookup.
No ids are hard-coded. The product is found at test time by its scenario SKU, and the expected name comes from PRODUCTS.hoodie.name.
The default admin stored session is used. The ticket names no specific permission, and there is no UI sign-in.
`check-types:e2e` exits 0. The spec is at e2e/tests/products/product-rename.spec.ts.
The spec only uses ProductPage locators and methods. The one inline call is `page.reload()`.
ProductPage has `readonly` fields initialised from `this.page` and uses `constructor(readonly page: Page) {}`.
It has an `// Arrange` comment and an `// Act & Assert` comment.
The story is a single test with two `test.step` stages.
The title "Staff renames a product and the new name is saved #e2e" describes the behaviour and carries the tag.
A header comment says what the spec covers and why the test reloads.
All assertions are web-first (toHaveValue, toContainText).
The original name is PRODUCTS.hoodie.name and the scenario is ORDERS_SCENARIO. The new name is a literal, but it is the ticket's input value, not a scenario value.
There is no cleanup code and no unique-name trick.
There are no explicit timeouts, no retries, no networkidle and no waitForLoadState.
Relative imports keep `.ts`. In the page object, only the `Page` type comes from @playwright/test.
The `gql` call is typed and there are no `any` types or casts.
The comments explain why: the title only updates once a save lands, and the reload is there to prove persistence.

structured_output.summary: I passed all 23 checklist items for this change. The spec reuses the orders scenario's E2E Hoodie, finds its id at test time through a read-only lookup by SKU, and renames the product through a new, conventional ProductPage page object. It then proves the save held by checking the name field and the page title after a reload, so it would fail if the rename never reached the server. The type check passes (exit 0). I found no blockers and no minors.
